subject: Operational decision: temporary throttle, quantization pilot & customer-facing note
messages:
From: Nick Hart <nick.hart@cartvista.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: emily.tan@cartvista.com
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected p95/p99 delta starting 07:45 PT - need short-term mitigation

Vanessa,

Quick note from our side — starting ~07:45 PT this morning we saw a sustained jump in p95 and p99 for the /generate endpoint that aligns with two traffic bursts from our EU region. Impact: user-facing latency up ~350-500ms at p95, some failed requests during spikes. Token consumption is within expected range. Attached: a small png showing the QPS and latency timeline.

We need to understand whether this is a routing/backpressure issue on your side or something in our traffic patterns. Can Redwood do any short-term throttling or fallback to a cheaper model variant for bursty requests? We can also temporarily drop non-essential batched requests on our side if that helps.

I escalated to Emily; tagging her for visibility — appreciate a quick read on mitigation options and a customer note we can post to our internal ops.

Thanks,
Nick Hart
VP, Operations — CartVista

Attachment: qps_spike_charts_20271107.png (image/png)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Nick Hart <nick.hart@cartvista.com>, emily.tan@cartvista.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 08:45:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95/p99 delta starting 07:45 PT - need short-term mitigation

Nick — thanks for the heads up and the chart. Looping in SRE (Ben), Product (Kimberly) and Eng (Karthik).

High-level asks from my side:
- Immediate: a short-lived throttle policy we can apply to CartVista's route (burst window cap) and a customer-friendly note explaining a temporary protective measure.
- Near-term: evaluate a quantization pilot + lighter-weight model variant for the heavy batched requests you mentioned (if quality impact acceptable).
- Ask for Redwood: confirmation we can do a per-customer burst cap without affecting other customers, and estimate rollback time.

Ben — can you confirm whether our autoscaler and routing policy can apply a per-route burst cap without a full config rollout? If not, what's the fastest safe mitigation (e.g., model fallback, token-per-request cap)?

Kimberly — can you map expected quality delta for a half-quantized variant or a faster open model for the workload in question?

Karthik — if SRE needs a temporary exception in instance pinning or routing, what's the risk window and timeline?

Nick/Emily — I’ll draft a short customer note once we have the technical mitigation. If you have a preferred wording that we can co-publish internally, share it and we’ll align.

I attached a draft MAP template (v2) we typically use for short escalations — I’ll update it with tasks after Ben/Karthik confirm.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_cartvista_v2.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Nick Hart <nick.hart@cartvista.com>, emily.tan@cartvista.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 09:12:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95/p99 delta starting 07:45 PT - need short-term mitigation

Quick update from SRE after an initial look at the telemetry:
- Cause signal: increased tail latency correlated with KV cache churn on GenAPI nodes serving CartVista’s partition. Likely root is a burst pattern where many sessions hit long-context flows simultaneously.
- Short-term mitigations we can enact immediately (order of preference):
  1) Apply a per-route burst allowance (throttle) to limit concurrent long-context requests from CartVista for 20 minutes. This is a runtime config change and can be pushed instantly to edge routers with no code deploy. Rollback is immediate.
  2) Route CartVista traffic to a compatible, lower-memory quantized instance group (same model family) — will reduce latency but may affect quality on edge cases. Requires a safe routing policy toggle; can be done within 10–15 minutes but will take monitoring.
  3) Per-request token cap (deny requests > N tokens) — last resort, more customer-impacting.

Operational impact: option (1) is minimal risk and buys time. Option (2) is medium risk; ops should declare quality impact and a measure for rollback. Option (3) is heavy-handed.

I propose we implement (1) now and run (2) as a canary on 1–2 nodes if CartVista approves.

Ben Carter
Sr. SRE — Redwood Inference

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Nick Hart <nick.hart@cartvista.com>, emily.tan@cartvista.com
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 12:03:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95/p99 delta starting 07:45 PT - need short-term mitigation

Thanks — quick product assessment:
- Quantization pilot: for CartVista’s workload we estimate a 10–18% latency improvement at p95 when using an int8-ish path, with a modest risk of hallucination on long-sequence summarization tasks. We can produce a short AB test (2–4% of traffic) to measure quality delta in ~24 hours.
- Lighter model variant: a fast open model (same family smaller config) will reduce tail but will cut semantic fidelity on multi-turn instructions. If CartVista traffic is mostly token-generation for suggestions/embeds, it may be acceptable.

Customer-facing note (draft):
"Redwood is applying a temporary burst-protection policy on your inference endpoint to restore latency SLOs. During the window you may see a small fraction of requests queued or routed to a faster model variant. We do not expect impact to correctness for typical short prompts; we will revert protections as soon as traffic normalizes"

If CartVista is comfortable, I recommend Ben apply the per-route throttle now and we run an int8 canary on 2 nodes while capturing a small sample of outputs for QA.

Kimberly Park
Product Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Nick Hart <nick.hart@cartvista.com>, emily.tan@cartvista.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95/p99 delta starting 07:45 PT - need short-term mitigation

Nick / Emily — thanks for the patience here. Quick execution summary and ask: 

What we did (completed at 15:10 PT today):
- Applied per-route burst cap for CartVista for a 30-minute window. This was an instantaneous runtime toggle; rollback is immediate.
- Started an int8 quantization canary on 2 instances for 10% of routed CartVista traffic; monitoring captured latency and a small QA sample.

Observed outcome (15:10–16:30 PT):
- p95 improved ~220ms vs peak and p99 reduced ~420ms. Error rate returned to baseline.
- QA sampling shows no material correctness regressions for short prompts; longer multi-turn summaries had two edge cases flagged by QA (we collected payloads securely).

Recommended next steps:
1) We keep the burst cap active for another 30 minutes and monitor; rollback earlier if CartVista sees client-side errors.
2) If you approve, we expand the int8 canary to 20% for 2 hours to gather more quality telemetry.
3) Redwood will deliver a short post-incident note with timeline and root-cause analysis draft by EOD tomorrow.

Please reply with a simple "approve" to expand the canary or "decline" to keep the throttle-only path. If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute bridge now.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks for the clear write-up and for moving fast. We approve expanding the int8 canary to 20% for 2 hours. Please keep us posted on QA findings; we’ll hold off on client-side throttles unless you instruct us.

A couple of asks on the MAP: can you add an explicit rollback threshold (p95 > baseline + 300ms sustained for 10 min) and a Spike RCA placeholder that references KV cache churn? That will help our internal ops playbook.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Nick
VP, Operations — CartVista
